meta.metric: candidate declarations are DECLARING FILES; augmentations (metadata.isAugmentation) are consulted only when no non-augmentation declaration exists
meta.resolutionRules: an edge is RESOLVED when the pool publishes ONE declaration AND the edge's own file can name it, by one of four rules whose per-run counts are printed and exported as resolutionProvenance: leaf-unique | qualified-endpoint (the edge's own <source>.<target> is a qualifiedName published in the same file) | lexical-local (the file declares the name and the reference is a BARE name; uses/contains are excluded because a member name is not proof of ownership) | lexical-import (the file binds the name to exactly one relative import that resolves to a declaring file). The first three replace a pool-wide-only rule that called 4,234 bindable edges ambiguous; the shape guard excludes 17 member-shape 'traps' where an imported leaf name is not the reference (import { join } from node:path says nothing about [1,2].join).
meta.note: The classes map IS the lane's declaration of what is done. A class that is nonzero and absent here fails the gate as UNDECLARED; a class above its ceiling fails as OVER CEILING. Ceilings are deliberately at the measured value: the backlog may not grow.

calls:ambiguous.rule: The lane's largest class. After the scope rules bind every edge whose own file can name the target, the residue is MEMBER names whose owner the edge does not name: `subscribe` (23 declaring files), `error` (41), `next` (19), `observable` (13), and the widest name on the pool `result` (294). A member call's receiver is a local variable, so no rule about the EDGE's file can bind it, and the family contract fixes leaf identity. Binding these needs the receiver's type or a qualified `Owner.member` target carried by the edge — an ontology decision that changes what every lane emits rather than a repair to this analyzer — so it is declared with a ceiling: it may not grow, it does not count as resolved, and its lever is named. 27,386 edges, down from 28,766 when only the pool-wide leaf rule existed (816 by the qualified endpoint, 1,928 by a bare name the file declares, 40 by a single relative import, the rest by the same rules on other types).

calls:external.rule: The declared-external marker and the four proofs it accepts: metadata.isExternalTarget plus metadata.externalReason is set only when the receiver is bound by an import/require of a BARE specifier that the nearest manifest lists as a dependency and this workspace does not publish (dependency-package), a Node builtin (builtin-module), a runtime global this file neither declares nor imports (runtime-global), or, in type positions, a name in the pinned TS_LIB_TYPE_NAMES table (builtin-lib-type). A file declaration, a relative import and a workspace package are excluded BEFORE the list is consulted. It is a STATEMENT about what the edge cannot bind here, not a resolution. Reasons on this run: dependency-package 15307, runtime-global 1146, builtin-lib-type 571, builtin-module 276. A ceiling is recorded because a marker that widens silently is worse than none: the lane's negative controls (a relative import and an 'rxjs' self-import stay UNMARKED) are what keep it honest, and this number is what shows if they stop working.

calls:externalUnreasoned.rule: A declared-external marker with no metadata.externalReason is a claim nobody can audit. Measured 0: all 17300 marked edges on this pool carry a reason, so the ceiling is 0 and a nonzero value fails the gate.

calls:targetless.rule: A relationship row with no target string binds nothing. Measured 0 for this type on this pool: a nonzero value means the analyzer emitted an edge with no endpoint, which is a defect and not a class, so the ceiling is 0.

calls:unresolved.rule: Receivers that are neither in-file declarations, nor external imports (marked above), nor runtime globals: test-runner globals declared outside the pool (`expect` 949, `it` 491, `describe` 218, `toHaveBeenCalled` 146, `toHaveBeenCalledWith` 81 — their call sites import NOTHING and the callee is a bare identifier, measured, so no import-based proof can reach them and a pinned test-runner table would be the only mechanism), member calls on LOCAL variables (`push` 2,296 on arrays and Subjects), and DOM member calls whose receiver the emission records no name for. Marking these would be a guess unless the name is pinned with provenance, and the marker's negative controls exist precisely to stop it. A repo-wide binding pass is the honest repair and this lane does not have one. 6,276 edges, unchanged by the scope rules because resolution and external marking are different questions.

imports:unresolved.rule: BY DESIGN, at 0% resolution, and no resolver can change it: the target is `<module>:<name>` — measured shapes on this pool: `vitest:describe`, `@angular/core:Component`, `rxjs/merge-map:mergeMap`. That is a module URI plus an exported name, not a symbol name, so nothing in the pool can ever publish it. The fleet arbiter counts this class as unresolved, which is why this lane cannot reach 100% under a rule that has no room for a declared design; this gate has room for it and shows the size (4626 edges, 5.5% of the pool's 84111).

references:ambiguous.rule: 33 edges, down from 346 after augmentations were made non-competing and 786 before that. The scope rules bind a type the file itself declares (`HostComponent`, `TestLocationService` — mocks, 249 edges) or imports by a single relative path. references:external.rule: The marker in TYPE position (996 edges): the target name is bound by an import of a bare dependency or a Node builtin (`import type { Foo } from "vitest"`), is rooted at a global type namespace whose head the file does not declare (`NodeJS.Timeout`, `Intl.NumberFormat`), is a pinned TS_LIB_TYPE_NAMES entry (`Promise`, `Partial`, `Record`, `HTMLElement`), or is a QUALIFIED name whose head is an external binding (`fs.Stats` under `import * as fs from "node:fs"` — worth +124 marks on its own, found by inspection after the first extension landed). Same exclusions first: a file declaration wins (a file-declared interface named `Record` is NOT marked), and a relative type import is not marked.

references:unresolved.rule: Composition MEASURED on the full pool (/tmp/ts-unresolved-lib-share.mts, 1011 unresolved type-position edges): 82 name a type some TypeScript lib file declares (`PropertyKey` 10, `HTMLAnchorElement` 7, `IteratorResult` 6), and 929 name something no lib file declares — dominated by TYPE PARAMETERS (`T` 621, `R` 46, `K` 30, `S` 17, `E` 13) and test-framework globals (`jasmine.Spy` 26, `jasmine.SpyObj` 3). Consequence, stated because it kills a plausible fix: extending the pinned TS_LIB_TYPE_NAMES table with the DOM set is worth 82 edges, 0.10% of the pool, and was measured and deliberately not done. A type parameter is a LOCAL binding: binding it needs type parameters published as symbols, and SUPPRESSING it instead is the uses-vs-references ontology contract question the lane has already declared OPEN (script/m14/spec/typescript-completeness.json) rather than decided by fiat.
